issues.detail: The historical k=3 claim says it applies with negligible diffusion, but its anchors are lines 85 and 105 and no selected fixed condition cites the explicit high-Peclet evidence at line 102. Add line 102 to a source locator for that applicability (or encode an experiment-only branch condition) and do not generalize it to the k=1 simulation branch.

previous_science_card.assessment: The source supports the self-similar spreading radius ratio Y=R(t)/R(t_ref)=(t/t_ref)^(1/(k+2)) for k=3 (experiment and simulation) and k=1 (simulation), with common conditions d=2, overdamped free spreading, and self-similar regime. The exponent beta=1/(k+2) is explicitly derived and confirmed. The control q=t/t_ref is a finite benchmark interval [1,10] within the positive self-similar variable, not a source physical boundary. The unknown amplitudes A and B are not set to 1; the ratio cancels them. The raw noisy radius is not claimed. The cluster is complete and case_authoring_ready is true.

mechanisms.statement: The suspension spreads self-similarly with radius R(t) ~ t^{1/(k+2)} for power law repulsion U ~ 1/r^k in overdamped free spreading, independent of dimension d.

previous_science_card.paper_scope: The paper studies overdamped spreading of particle suspensions under repulsive power law potentials U ~ 1/r^k, deriving self-similar density profiles and radius growth R(t) ~ t^{1/(k+2)}. It includes experiments with magnetized colloids (k=3) and molecular dynamics simulations for various k, focusing on density profiles and memory retention. The selected cluster is the self-similar free-spreading radius ratio for k=3 and k=1 in 2D.
